notes:
Context and summary:
- Product: HighTide builds a cloud contact center platform used by e-commerce + telco customers. Evaluating LLM-based agent assist + RAG to reduce SLA breaches and speed time-to-resolution.
- POC goal: replace first-draft agent responses + automated ticket summarization + one-click tool-calls into their internal ticketing and billing systems. Need citations + source links for auditing.
- Scale concerns: typical daily load 40k conversations, peak spikes up to 18k concurrent active chats during sales events. Need graceful degradation and fallback routing.
- Latency/throughput targets: median assistant RTT < 350ms for single-turn responses; embedding generation for search < 200ms per doc at 500qps baseline. Batch strategies welcome.
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high; interested in quantization and batching recommendations from Optimize. Aim to keep per-conversation inference cost stable under spikes.
- Model preferences: prefer open/quantized models for on-prem/dedicated buckets; hosted for quick rollout. Interested in Redwood's model catalog with verified perf profiles.
- RAG specifics requested: citation-first results (quoted snippets + doc link), freshness guarantees (TTL on vector index + recency-based boosting), multi-source retrieval: kb articles + product changelogs + transcripts. Must support per-source provenance.
- Tooling: function/tool calling to open internal tickets (ticket.create), escalate (ticket.escalate), run billing lookups (billing.query). Need secure credentials handling (KMS/HSM).
- Security: SSO (SAML), enterprise audit logs, retention controls per-customer policy, EU data residency for EU customers.
- Recent timeline:
  - 2026-02-12: Initial inbound from IR team -> AE (Ravi) opened lead.
  - 2026-02-19: Intro call (ff_20260226_T2A9ZQ) w/ Head of Ops (Dana Ruiz) - discussed spike profile and RAG requirements.
  - 2026-02-26: Technical deep-dive with SE (Lena) + infra (ff_20260226_T2A9ZQ). Demo of Redwood hosted API; asked about KV cache and prefix caching.
  - 2026-03-03: Sent baseline POC plan + pricing (drive doc). Customer requested dedicated pool option for production tenants.
  - 2026-03-05: Security touchpoint (ff_20260305_R4N1BX). Provided SOC2 evidence + data residency note; security requested KMS integration details.
  - 2026-03-09: Ingested sample KB (12k articles), set up initial vector index and two retrievers (semantic + title exact). Running first recall evals.
  - 2026-03-10: Load test scheduled (2-week POC). Baseline metrics captured.
- Quotes / paraphrases from stakeholders:
  - "We cannot ship agent-suggested responses that lack citations — legal will block it." (Dana, Head of Ops)
  - "If you can show graceful fallback at 80% of peak, we can avoid full private deployment initially." (CTO, Miguel Alvarez)
- POC acceptance criteria:
  - Citation trace for every suggested response with source confidence score.
  - 95th percentile response latency within SLO under 75% of predicted peak.
  - Ticket summarization F1 > 0.78 on labeled set.
  - Secure tool-calls with rotation of credentials via KMS.
- Open technical questions / blockers in thread:
  - Which vector DB will Redwood route to for low-latency multi-region reads? Customer evaluating Pinecone vs self-hosted Milvus.
  - How does Redwood handle per-tenant cache invalidation when KB updates? Need TTL + invalidation hooks.
  - Procurement needs a pricing deck that separates Hosted vs Dedicated capacity costs for predictable ARR modeling.
- Next steps (short):
  - Finish 2-week load POC (team: Lena + infra) and capture 95/99 latency under simulated events.
  - Produce security appendix (KMS/HSM details) and hand to HighTide InfoSec.
  - Provide SOW draft for Dedicated capacity pilot (Michael to own).
